key_insight: A matrix-free, high-order phase-field fracture solver can efficiently capture steep crack-damage gradients while coupling visco-elasto-plasticity and fracture at micromechanical scales.
engineering_relevance: This enables more scalable and GPU-ready fracture simulations for inelastic materials, improving predictive micromechanical testing of particle-matrix composites and similar solids.
method: Implemented the Peric & Dettmer visco-elastoplastic constitutive framework in an open-source solid mechanics library.
Used matrix-free operators with high-order finite elements and p-multigrid preconditioning on GPUs.
Introduced a rheological fracture element assembled in series to separate inelastic and fracture effects at homogenization scales.
evidence_signal: The approach was evaluated through tensile and compressive simulations of synthetic particle-matrix microstructures on an El Capitan prototype, reproducing characteristic inelastic responses and crack propagation patterns.
watch_item: High-order matrix-free phase-field models can be computationally efficient, but they still require careful calibration of length scales, constitutive parameters, and solver/preconditioner robustness for complex microstructures.
paper_title: Matrix-free phase-field modeling of fracture in micromechanical testing simulations of inelastic materials
